chapter.title: How to Dehypnotize Yourself from False Beliefs

concepts.title: Belief revision requires testing the premise
concepts.content: A restrictive conclusion can be challenged when new experience contradicts it. Adler’s school-math example portrays a successful blackboard solution disconfirming a perceived fixed incapacity.

concepts.thesis: A restrictive conclusion can be challenged when new experience contradicts it.

terms.primary: Belief revision requires testing the premise
terms.definition: A restrictive conclusion can be challenged when new experience contradicts it.

concepts.author_mechanism: Adler’s school-math example portrays a successful blackboard solution disconfirming a perceived fixed incapacity.
concepts.conditions_and_limits: One success or failure does not establish a lifelong personal trait.
concepts.application: Choose a belief that predicts a behavior, then seek small fair tests with observable results.
concepts.common_misreading: Treating a conceptual or anecdotal explanation as a universal causal law, without evaluating context, skills or competing explanations.
concepts.alternative_explanation: Practice, teacher feedback and changing expectations can each affect results.
concepts.ethical_clinical_cautions: One success or failure does not establish a lifelong personal trait.
concepts.substantive_paraphrase: A restrictive conclusion can be challenged when new experience contradicts it. In the revised book this is explained through adler’s school-math example portrays a successful blackboard solution disconfirming a perceived fixed incapacity. A careful application would be: Choose a belief that predicts a behavior, then seek small fair tests with observable results.
concepts.evidence_assessment: The book contains this discussion. Scientific generality is not established by citation to the book.

concepts.title: False belief versus dishonest pretending
concepts.content: The book distinguishes challenging a possibly erroneous self-judgment from fabricating external achievements. The chapter explicitly rejects superficial fake-it-until-you-make-it behavior in favor of testing the truth of self-beliefs.

concepts.title: Inferiority feeling versus unequal skill
concepts.content: Being less capable at one task does not logically make a person inferior in overall human worth. The text contrasts professional domains of a golfer and surgeon to show the error of making task comparisons global.

author_practices.title: Dehypnotization relaxation imagery
author_practices.content: The revised book prescribes: Sit or lie comfortably and soften muscles for about 5 minutes. Imagine heavy concrete limbs (Mental Picture 1). Imagine loosened marionette strings (Mental Picture 2). Remember a safe, peaceful scene with sensory detail (Mental Picture 3). Timing: at least 30 minutes daily; initial approximately 5-minute muscle relaxation
